title: Canonical top cohomology comparison for derived module pullback
statement:
Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $n\in\mathbf Z$, and $C\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category] with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>n$. Use the canonical truncation $\tau_C:C\to H^n(C)[-n]$ of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], and ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For an $\mathcal O_S$-module $M$, let $c_{g,M}:Lg^*(M[0])\to(g^*M)[0]$ be the comparison normalized as the transpose of the ordinary pullback unit [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. Then $H^i(Lg^*C)=0$ for $i>n$, $H^0(c_{g,M})$ is an isomorphism, and
$$\kappa_{g,C}:H^n(Lg^*C)\xrightarrow{H^n(Lg^*\tau_C)}H^n(Lg^*(H^n(C)[-n]))\xrightarrow{H^0(c_{g,H^n(C)})}g^*H^n(C)$$
is an isomorphism (the second arrow uses the canonical shift comparison). It is natural for every morphism $u:C\to D$ between objects with cohomology zero above $n$:
$$\kappa_{g,D}H^n(Lg^*u)=g^*H^n(u)\kappa_{g,C}.$$
For every $h:T'\to T$, under the canonical derived composition isomorphism [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] and the ordinary composition isomorphism $c^{\rm ord}_{g,h}:h^*g^*\cong(gh)^*$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition],
$$\kappa_{gh,C}=c^{\rm ord}_{g,h,H^n(C)}\,h^*(\kappa_{g,C})\,\kappa_{h,Lg^*C}.$$
No lower cohomological bound, flatness, quasi-coherence, or finite rank is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing: dual of (1) and dual of the truncation argument in the proof of (2), applied to the right-exact module pullback. The normalization, naturality and composition formulas are the agent assembly from this argument and the canonical pullback comparisons.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing C. The standard upper-bound description gives an isomorphic representative K with K^i=0 for i>n. Apply the bounded-above flat replacement theorem on the site of opens of S, with N=n, to obtain a quasi-isomorphism P→K with flat terms and P^i=0 for i>n. This P is K-flat by the bounded-above-flat criterion. Hence Lg^*C is canonically represented by the termwise pullback g^*P. Write ε_{g,P}:Lg^*Q(P)→Q(g^*P) for this comparison. In all uses of ε choose the counit pinned to the derived adjunction in the statement; its evaluation on M[0] is c_{g,M}. The definition of derived pullback computes that counit invertibly on K-flat representatives.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution (upper bound preserved); Cohomology Tags 06YD, 06YJ

proof.text: Ordinary module pullback preserves cokernels: for A→B with cokernel E and any target module N, its adjunction gives Hom(g^*E,N)=Hom(E,g_*N), the equalizer of Hom(B,g_*N)⇉Hom(A,g_*N), and hence the equalizer of Hom(g^*B,N)⇉Hom(g^*A,N). This is precisely the universal property of the cokernel of g^*A→g^*B. In particular the induced map coker(g^*d_P^{n-1})→g^*coker(d_P^{n-1}) is an isomorphism, characterized by its composite with the quotient out of g^*P^n.

Since (g^*P)^i=0 for i>n, its cohomology is zero above n, and H^n(g^*P)=coker(g^*d_P^{n-1}). Also H^n(P)=coker(d_P^{n-1}). Step 2 therefore gives an isomorphism θ_{g,P}:H^n(Lg^*Q(P))→g^*H^n(P): first apply H^n(ε_{g,P}), then the cokernel isomorphism. Explicitly, if π:P^n→H^n(P) is the quotient, θ_{g,P} is the map induced by g^*π after the representative comparison. This proves the required upper vanishing for C. It uses no lower bound on P.

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing, dual upper-bound argument, computed on the flat representative

proof.text: Apply step 1 with n=0 and C=M[0], using a resolution q:P→M[0] with P^i=0 for i>0. Naturality of the left-derived counit gives c_{g,M}∘Lg^*Q(q)=Q(g^*q)∘ε_{g,P}, with the single-complex identifications understood. On H^0 the map on the right is induced by g^*(q^0):g^*P^0→g^*M. Since q is a quasi-isomorphism, H^0(q):coker(d_P^{-1})→M is an isomorphism. By step 2, H^0(Q(g^*q)) is g^*H^0(q) after the cokernel identification and is an isomorphism. Thus H^0(c_{g,M}) is an isomorphism. This verifies the particular normalized map, rather than merely constructing an isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Tag 06YJ, lemma-derived-base-change, derived counit on a flat resolution; right-exact cokernel calculation

proof.text: On the model P of step 1, the top truncation projection is the complex map p:P→H^n(P)[-n], whose degree-n component is π and whose other components are zero. Evaluate naturality of ε_g on p. The pinned shift compatibility identifies its value on H^n(P)[-n] with c_{g,H^n(P)}[-n]. Consequently the composite defining κ_{g,Q(P)} is exactly θ_{g,P}: on cokernels it is induced by g^*π. This is an isomorphism by step 3. Transporting along Q(P)≅C gives exactly the stated κ_{g,C}, because both the truncation projection and the counit are natural under this isomorphism. In particular H^n(Lg^*τ_C) is invertible as well, since its composite with the isomorphism of step 4 is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; dual truncation argument of 05TC; pinned counit shift square

proof.text: The truncation projection is natural for all derived morphisms between objects bounded above by n. Indeed smart truncation on complexes is functorial, carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and hence descends through the derived localization. On an upper-bounded representative its top quotient is H^n[-n]. Thus τ_D∘u=H^n(u)[-n]∘τ_C, also when u is only a derived morphism. Naturality of c_g is the naturality of the one fixed counit at maps of single complexes. Applying H^nLg^* to the first equation and then counit naturality yields κ_{g,D}H^n(Lg^*u)=g^*H^n(u)κ_{g,C}. The shift comparisons are compatible with that counit. On a shifted single module N[-n], κ is H^0(c_{g,N}), since its top truncation projection is the identity.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; descent of functorial smart truncation through localization

proof.text:
First record composition on a single module M. Apply the composition theorem for canonical single pullback comparisons with f=h:T′→T, g=g:T→S and N=M. In Lean order it gives γ_{M[0]}.hom ≫ p_{gh}(M) = Lh^*(p_g(M)) ≫ p_h(g^*M) ≫ (pullbackComp(h,g)_M.hom)[0], where γ:Lh^*Lg^*→L(gh)^* is the chosen derived composition isomorphism of the statement and pullbackComp(h,g):h^*g^*≅(gh)^* is the ordinary composition isomorphism c^{ord}_{g,h}. These p's are the c's of the statement. By the single-comparison node, p_a(N) is the selected left-derived counit at N[0] followed by the single-complex identification and the adjunction-preserving tensor-to-ordinary identification. The adjunction-transpose theorem with M=a^*N and the map id_{a^*N} says that the transpose of p_a(N) under the selected adjunction La^*⊣Ra_* is the ordinary unit N→a_*a^*N in degree zero followed by (a_*a^*N)[0]→Ra_*((a^*N)[0]). That is exactly the normalization of c_{a,N}. Since transposition is a bijection, p_a(N)=c_{a,N}. Hence
c_{gh,M}∘γ_{M[0]}=(c^{ord}_{g,h,M})[0]∘c_{h,g^*M}∘Lh^*(c_{g,M}).
By the counit shift and composition shift compatibilities, the same equation holds with M[-n] in place of M[0] and c[-n] in place of c.

source.place: Tag 0D5S, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; existing canonical single comparison composition and adjunction transpose

proof.text:
Put M=H^n(C), B=M[-n], and B′=(g^*M)[-n]. Let v:Lg^*C→B′ be Lg^*(τ_C) followed by c_{g,M}[-n], using the shift comparison. By definition H^n(v)=κ_{g,C}. Its source and target are bounded above by n by step 3. Apply step 6 for h to this particular v. Since κ_{h,B′}=H^0(c_{h,g^*M}), it gives
h^*(κ_{g,C})κ_{h,Lg^*C}=H^0(c_{h,g^*M})H^n(Lh^*v).
Postcompose by c^{ord}_{g,h,M}. Substitute v and the shifted single equation of step 7. Naturality of γ at τ_C moves γ past Lh^*Lg^*(τ_C). The resulting expression is H^n(c_{gh,M}[-n])H^n(L(gh)^*τ_C)H^n(γ_C)=κ_{gh,C}H^n(γ_C). This is exactly the requested composition formula under the specified canonical composition isomorphism. No inverse to c_{g,M} in the derived category has been used; such an inverse generally does not exist.
